title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
# Product of Array Except Self

Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` where `answer[i]` equals the product of every element of `nums` except `nums[i]`.

The product of any prefix or suffix of `nums` is **guaranteed** to fit in a **32-bit** integer.

Your algorithm must run in `O(n)` time and must not use division.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [1,2,3,4]
**Output:** [24,12,8,6]

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [-1,1,0,-3,3]
**Output:** [0,0,9,0,0]

## Constraints:

*   `2 <= nums.length <= 10^5`
*   `-30 <= nums[i] <= 30`
*   The product of any prefix or suffix of `nums` is **guaranteed** to fit in a **32-bit** integer.

tests.description: Single zero should produce exactly one non-zero output

solutions.name: Prefix and Suffix Products
solutions.description:
## Approach

For each position, the answer is the product of everything to its left times the product of everything to its right. Store the left products directly in the output array, then scan from right to left while carrying one running suffix product.

## Key Insight

This is the canonical solution because it respects both important constraints: O(n) time and no division. The output array is allowed, so only the running suffix variable counts as extra working memory.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1) extra space, excluding the required output array

solutions.name: Two Arrays (Prefix and Suffix)
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use two explicit helper arrays: one for products before each index and one for products after each index. Multiplying the two arrays gives the answer.

## Key Insight

This is less space-efficient than the optimized version, but it is valuable as a teaching step because it exposes the exact prefix/suffix invariant before compressing the suffix array into one variable.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)

solutions.name: Bidirectional Single-Loop Sweep
solutions.description:
## Approach

Initialize every output slot to 1. Walk one index from the left and one index from the right in the same loop. Before multiplying the current number into a running product, write that running product into the matching output position.

## Key Insight

The left running product gives the product of values before the current left index, while the right running product gives the product of values after the current right index. Updating both directions in one loop keeps the same prefix/suffix invariant as the canonical solution while staying O(n), division-free, and O(1) in extra working memory.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1) extra space, excluding the required output array
